purpose: Provenance of source ancestry that resolved native byte-exact Nemu64 audio.dll integer envelope reconstruction. Research only; no target source edits made by this report task.
finding: UltraHLE 1.0.0 src/SLIST.C envmix_zelda and envmix_mario are direct source ancestors of Nemu FD10 and F8E0, supported by distinctive identical code structure and byte-exact compilation after Nemu-specific adaptations. The same Zelda loop structure also resolves Nemu 10060.

mirror.role: Archival mirror; uploader explicitly disclaims author affiliation. This is not claimed to be an official author repository.

authorship_and_notices.archive_license_file: No LICENSE/COPYING file or general source license grant was found in the downloaded archive.
archive_notice_scan: src/ULTRA.H:81-85 discusses restrictions on the separate X-Engine/Glide component, not the envelope implementation.
src/VERSION.H:10-14 defines an empty secondary notice for RELEASE builds and a private/nonpublic distribution notice for non-RELEASE builds.
Several UI source files have 1999 Epsilon and RealityMan copyright comments.

google_code_project_metadata.interpretation: This is uploader-supplied project metadata; it does not itself establish a license grant by the original authors. Preserve the original copyright instead of presenting the historical source as definitively Apache licensed.

authorship_and_notices.other_mirror_license: The unrelated modern emu-russia/UltraHLE repository displays CC0-1.0, but was not used as the source and does not establish the license of this archive.
authorship_and_notices.scope: Recorded factual provenance and notices only; no independent legal conclusion.

historical_corroboration.assessment: OHLE project announcement says its starting point was the last known supposedly leaked UltraHLE source by RealityMan and Epsilon. This corroborates contemporaneous source circulation; the current research has not verified that release archive against the later Google Code archive.
historical_corroboration.zip_date_caveat: SLIST.C ZIP timestamp is 1999-01-26 22:50:00 without a timezone. ZIP timestamps alone do not authenticate authorship or release date.

distinctive_evidence: Count conversion precedes input/output address conversions.
Function-wide i,j,jn,lx,rx and lt,rt temporaries; chained lt=rt sample load.
Three paths: dry fixed, auxiliary fixed, eight-sample ramped.
Separate lx/rx accumulation temporaries with sample clamps commented out.
Gain updates occur after each full eight-sample block, clamp to 0..65535, zero corresponding ramp.
The silence predicate repeats the right gain test and omits the right ramp; there is no envelope state writeback.
adaptations: Global sst storage becomes the Nemu AudioContext parameter and its buffer pointer.
Runtime sound logging is absent in the target.
Function/field names mapped to reconstructed Nemu names.
function_relationships.native_result: 848/848 raw bytes identical, including alignment, zero relocations.

distinctive_evidence: Eight int envelope values are shifted left one before use.
Ramp == 65535 comparison occurs after doubling, with redundant >0 predicate.
Function-wide i,j,jn,lt,rt; chained sample assignment and separate destination += operations.
Three fixed/ramped paths, eight-sample blocks, signed ramp directions and target clipping.
All eight values are shifted back and saved in the same order.
adaptations: Global sst storage becomes the Nemu AudioContext parameter and its buffer pointer.
Runtime sound logging is absent in the target.
The archive silence predicate ends with !rtmul==0 after !rtmul; target evidence instead requires the duplicated !rtmul condition without ==0. This is an explicit Nemu-specific source difference.
function_relationships.native_result: 1072/1072 raw bytes identical, including alignment, zero relocations.

function_relationships.relationship: No identical unsigned-gain function was found in this archive. Reusing the historically evidenced local-variable and loop structure, while retaining target-recovered unsigned gain/ramp behavior, solved the implementation.
